# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The change stops the analyzer from crashing on bad keys. In both member-collection loops of TypeCollector, a member whose key kind does not match the others is now skipped right after MsgPack005 is reported. Duplicate int or string keys no longer go to Dictionary.Add, which would throw. The change also adds analyzer tests for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types, two run-time round-trip tests, and a README section. Separately, it changes the depth limit check in MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep from `>=` to `>`.
story.why: Issue 2234 says the analyzer stops working for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types since 3.1.1. The diff implies the cause was an exception from Dictionary.Add on duplicate keys, which ends the whole analysis. The diff never says so directly, and none of the TypeCollector edits mention SuppressSourceGeneration. If suppressed types were skipped by some other path, this diff does not show it.
touches_beyond_requirement: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs: the max-depth comparison changes from `>=` to `>`. That lets deserialization go one level deeper than MaximumObjectGraphDepth. It is in untrusted-input handling and has nothing to do with the analyzer issue.
README.md: a new user-facing section that lists which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types.
The duplicate-key and mixed-key changes also affect normal, non-suppressed types, because the same code paths are shared.
story.confidence_overview: Medium that the TypeCollector edits remove an analyzer crash on duplicate or mixed keys. Low-to-medium that this is the whole fix for 'the analyzer does not work': the diff does not show the regression mechanism, and we cannot tell whether the MsgPack004/015/003 tests failed before this change. High that the MessagePackSecurity edit is an unrelated weakening of a security limit.

claims.text: Duplicate int keys and duplicate string keys are no longer passed to Dictionary.Add. Only the first member with a given key is kept, so the analyzer no longer throws, and the existing MsgPack005 report still fires.

breaker.reason: Two of the four cited hunks (src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs lines 1163-1166 and 1179-1182) are in the field-collection loop, but none of the three named tests in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs (lines 81-100, 103-122, 147-166) declare any fields; all three only test auto-properties, leaving the field duplicate-key paths and property-field key collisions completely untested. Additionally, none of the changed code in TypeCollector.cs is specific to SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

claims.text: A member whose key kind (int or string) differs from the other members is skipped right after MsgPack005 is reported. This avoids the null dereference of `intKey!.Value` or `stringKey!` further down.
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
evidence: test `MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure` blocked by the machine (not evidence either way)

breaker.reason: In the property loop (src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs line 1008), stringKey! at lines 1030 and 1035 was already guarded by 'else if (stringKey is not null)' at line 1028, so the added continue never avoided a null stringKey! dereference there. Furthermore, the sole named test MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure (tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 125-144) only tests properties with an int key followed by a string key, so it never exercises the cited field-loop hunk (TypeCollector.cs lines 1145-1149) or the '!isIntKey && stringKey == null' branch in either loop.

claims.text: The change also edits deserialization depth limiting in MessagePackSecurity. That edit is not needed by the requirement and changes run-time security behavior.

breaker.reason: Checked src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs lines 231-236: DepthStep changes 'reader.Depth >= this.MaximumObjectGraphDepth' to 'reader.Depth > this.MaximumObjectGraphDepth', altering run-time deserialization depth enforcement even though REQ-2234 only concerns analyzer behavior with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

claims.text: The README documents which analyzer rules do and do not apply to suppressed types. MsgPack012 is listed as reported, but no test covers it.

breaker.reason: Checked README.md lines 1620-1632 against tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 20-192: README.md lists MsgPack004, MsgPack005, MsgPack015, MsgPack003, and MsgPack012 as reported and MsgPack011, MsgPack016, and MsgPack017 as not reported, and no test in the diff checks MsgPack012.

They also check that no diagnostics (including MsgPack011/016/017) are reported for a valid suppressed type with private and init members. The diff does not show whether the 004/015/003 tests failed before the fix.
